implemented_coverage.notes: Promoted as a recent Qwen3 MoE causal LM published basis with explicit hf_causal preset, public WikiText-103 release-profile H100 CUDA report, runtime manifest, and signed evidence pack from run 20260613Tqwen330ba3bH100All8. The fixture uses bfloat16/low-CPU-memory loading, disabled optional Hugging Face loading-info collection, automatic device placement across all eight H100 80GB GPUs, and scoped attention/router/shared-expert guard scans. This is no-op preservation evidence; it is not a benchmark-quality, fine-tuning, deployment, exhaustive expert-bank, or MoE routing-quality claim. A restricted four-GPU diagnostic lane failed and is intentionally not used as publication evidence.

Promoted as a recent Gemma 4 multimodal MoE published basis using the explicit hf_multimodal path, pinned public VQAv2 image-text materialization, release-profile H100 CUDA report, runtime manifest, and signed evidence pack from run 20260613Tgemma426ba4bH100A. This is no-op preservation evidence; it is not a benchmark-quality, fine-tuning, audio, or MoE routing-quality claim.

Promoted as a Mixtral MoE causal LM published basis with explicit hf_causal preset, release-profile H100 CUDA report, runtime manifest, and signed evidence pack. The preset keeps the full guard scan surface while using BF16, automatic device placement, low-CPU-memory loading, disabled optional HF loading-info collection, and a skipped optional guard-overhead check for large-model resource discipline.
Generic Llama-family profile handling is first-class. OpenLLaMA and TinyLlama now provide ungated declared support lanes, while access-gated vendor checkpoints remain omitted.

Shared qwen-family heuristics cover aliases beyond the declared text-only Qwen2, Qwen2.5 14B, Qwen3, and Qwen3.5 9B public lanes. Qwen3.5 2B now has published image-text evidence through hf_multimodal and pinned public VQAv2 materialization; Qwen3.5 4B remains prepared but blocked after strict-prompt H100 sanity reproduced zero exact-answer VQA accuracy.
Yi is treated as a RoPE decoder family in profile and adapter-auto logic.
Phi-family selectors are first-class. Phi-4 now has a declared text-only lane via the reasoning-plus pilot, while multimodal Phi-4 remains backlog-only.

Gemma-family selectors and loaders are first-class for compatible local or user-supplied checkpoints. Repo-declared Gemma support is limited to Gemma 4 lanes with public evidence: Gemma 4 E2B text-only plus Gemma 4 12B and 26B-A4B image-text public bases. Gemma 3 and Gemma 3n hosted checkpoints are omitted from the repo support/promotion inventory because their Hugging Face pages are access-gated under Gemma terms.

These families are available through shared GPT-style loader and profile paths rather than dedicated public support lanes. The catalog intentionally avoids naming the common OPT-1.3B hosted checkpoint because it is not Apache-2.0 or MIT licensed.
GPT-OSS rides the shared GPT-style profile path, with an explicit HF causal loader hint for the published open-weight checkpoint.
Falcon 7B now has a declared support lane; remaining Falcon-family coverage is available through adapter-auto heuristics and variant-path tests.

Family visibility currently comes from adapter-auto heuristics only. The catalog intentionally avoids naming the hosted GLM-4 9B Chat checkpoint because its public license is custom/restricted rather than Apache-2.0 or MIT.

DeepSeek distill checkpoints continue to share the qwen-family route. Oversized FP8 checkpoint-specific repo hooks and shipped configs were removed after bring-up showed that they do not fit the supported hardware/runtime path.
Loader and adapter-auto support exceeds the public BERT / RoBERTa support lane.

Concrete loader families exist beyond the public FLAN-T5 base seq2seq basis; mBART/PEGASUS/Marian still need dedicated presets and public evidence before they become declared support lanes. The catalog intentionally avoids naming CC-BY-4.0-only hosted checkpoints because they are outside the repo's strict Apache-2.0/MIT named-checkpoint policy.
